clue.text: Book for the picture show

parts.note: a book whose purpose is to display photographs or stamps; 'picture show' also suggests a cinema, the misleading reading

explanation.surface: Someone looking for a book to go with a film screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture show' reads as an old phrase for the cinema, but here it is a book in which pictures are shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo album is a bound book made for keeping and showing pictures.

clue.text: Robust seamen often are so described

definitions.meaning: the naval rating AB stands for this phrase, said of an ordinary trained sailor

explanation.surface: A remark on how sailors tend to be labelled.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy, AB is an able seaman, traditionally written out with this hyphenated adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust here means physically healthy and strong, which is the plain sense of fit in body.

clue.text: Launch report on cricket side

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a blast
the off side is one half of a cricket field, opposite the leg side

explanation.surface: News of a cricket team's opening, or a story about a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link here: the off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket's launch is its moment of lift-off from the pad.

clue.text: Human resources that feminists fight against?

definitions.meaning: the workforce available, people as a resource
read as two words, male dominance, which feminism opposes

explanation.surface: A wry question about what feminism campaigns against in the personnel department.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as MAN POWER for the second sense: the power of men.
explanation.definitionFit: Human resources means the people available for work, the available labour force.

clue.text: Sally is involved with transport curriculum

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of Sally are mixed

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Sally is busy with a course of study about getting around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved' rearranges SALLY into SYLLA; 'with' simply joins it to BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A curriculum and this word both name the outline of topics taught on a course.

clue.text: Type of pudding served as seconds before now

parts.note: ago means in time past, before the present

explanation.surface: Second helpings of a pudding dished up earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like second helpings but just gives S; 'served as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago pudding is a classic British milk dessert made from palm starch grains.

clue.text: People living around pubs

definitions.meaning: a person's neighbourhood pub is called their local, so the plural is pubs

explanation.surface: Residents of a district with pubs all around them.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one's 'local' is the nearest pub one regularly drinks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a neighbourhood are its natives, the people who live nearby.

clue.text: Sailor capsized, boom shattered — it's hollow-stemmed

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters for the sailor are flipped

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the letters of boom are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sailor's boat turns over and its boom breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns AB to BA; 'shattered' rearranges BOOM into MBOO.
explanation.definitionFit: This giant grass has notably hollow, jointed stems, so the description identifies it.

clue.text: Small child's slide

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A little one's playground slide.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after child is a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To slide uncontrollably on a slippery surface is the sense of this verb, as a car does on ice.

clue.text: Fifty winning scholarship

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
winning money, as in earning a wage

explanation.surface: A fifty-point win secures a scholarship award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scholarship' reads as an award but means erudition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship in the sense of deep academic knowledge is a synonym for erudition gained by study.

clue.text: Yet it's not the place for a deep sleep

definitions.text: Yet it's not the place for a deep sleep

parts.words: Yet it's not the place for a deep sleep
parts.note: the sea floor is very deep and is called a bed, but nobody sleeps there

explanation.surface: A remark that somewhere is unsuitable for a sound night's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep' and 'bed' are taken literally: the floor of the sea lies deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor of the sea is a bed in the geographical sense and lies at great depth.

clue.text: Talks about port transport

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talks go round the port

parts.note: chats are informal talks
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Discussions concerning shipping goods through a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like a verb with port, but it is the definition: the vehicles themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Chariots were horse-drawn vehicles, an ancient means of transport.

clue.text: Page in script of Cinderella

parts.note: a page is a boy servant; in the pantomime, Cinderella's friend is the page-boy character with this name

explanation.surface: Looking up a particular page of a play's script.
explanation.walkthrough: A British pantomime is a comic family stage show at Christmas; in Cinderella the page is a stock character named after his uniform's fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: The role of the pageboy in pantomime Cinderella carries this name, from the rows of fasteners on his livery.

clue.text: Homeless pet seen in street light shadow

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
to shadow someone is to dog them, follow closely

explanation.surface: An abandoned animal spotted in the shade of a street lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is a link; 'street light' looks like one item but splits into two pieces, and 'shadow' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal without an owner or a home, wandering about, is exactly what this phrase means.

clue.text: Convey ecstasy

definitions.meaning: to carry from place to place
a ... of joy is a state of rapture

explanation.surface: An instruction to communicate a feeling of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Convey is a synonym in the carrying sense; ecstasy matches the literary sense of rapture or overwhelming emotion.

clue.text: Do as you're told and become a priest!

definitions.meaning: holy orders are conferred at ordination, so a priest-to-be receives them

explanation.surface: A stern instruction to obey and join the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeying means accepting commands; in church language one receives holy orders on ordination as a cleric.

clue.text: Where to obtain counter-intelligence?

parts.note: counter-intelligence suggests spying, but here it is facts got at a counter

explanation.surface: A question about where to find spy-catching services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-intelligence' looks like espionage but means intelligence (news) available over a counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A help point in a station or shop is a counter where visitors get facts and directions.

clue.text: Time to dine on stews

indicators.note: to stew is to cook something mixed up, so the letters of to dine on are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mealtime arrives with stew on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stews' looks like the food but is a verb rearranging TO DINE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, the middle of the day, is a time of day named in this old poetic word.

clue.text: You're probably surprised when they go up

definitions.text: You're probably surprised when they go up

parts.words: You're probably surprised when they go up
parts.note: raised brows on the face signal astonishment

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about things whose rise causes surprise, like prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the hair above one's eyes is the classic facial expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Ring, evidently embarrassed — it shows shame

parts.note: a ring of metal can be a flat disc, as with a washer
someone visibly embarrassed is red in the face
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blushing ring-bearer shows that something is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evidently' means the embarrassment is visible, hence a flushed face; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour or disgrace is the sense of shame here, a loss of reputation.

clue.text: One's learned to park a vehicle in street

indicators.note: the vehicle parked in the street goes inside its letters

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Instructions on parking a vehicle in a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's learned' means one who is learned (adjective, two syllables), not past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of great erudition is a learned person.

clue.text: I tarry, resorting to curiosity

indicators.note: read as re-sorting, sorting again, so the letters of I tarry are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lingers at a holiday resort out of curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorting' is read as re-sorting; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A curiosity in the sense of an unusual object is an uncommon item, a collector's oddity.

clue.text: Bank that may appear in the current recession

definitions.text: Bank that may appear in the current recession

parts.words: Bank that may appear in the current recession
parts.note: a ridge of sand emerges when the tide or flow of water recedes

explanation.surface: A financial institution that could emerge during today's economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank', 'current' and 'recession' all sound financial; they mean a shoal, a water flow and its retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of sand in a river or sea is a bank that is exposed at low water.

clue.text: British? Always time for a drink!

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A Briton who reckons it is always time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Any liquid for drinking other than water is a synonym for a drink in formal use.

clue.text: Insult that's found on the wire

definitions.meaning: ... wire carries sharp points along its length

explanation.surface: An insult that has been sent by telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wire' suggests a news wire or telegraph; it means fencing wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting, wounding remark is a gibe; a sharp point on fencing wire shares the name.

clue.text: Direction taken by the astronaut

indicators.note: the letters are held by the words the astronaut, contained within them

explanation.surface: The course flown by a spaceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' picks the letters out of thE ASTronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cardinal points of the compass, a direction.

clue.text: Cure for love-sickness?

parts.note: against doting, so a remedy for infatuation

explanation.surface: A question about how to recover from a broken heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ANTI-DOTE: to dote is to love excessively, so this is something against doting.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that counteracts a poison is a cure, and the split reading makes it one against excessive fondness.

clue.text: Two adjacent pieces in a gradual sequence

definitions.meaning: one piece beside another piece, read literally as a phrase
gradually, a little at a time

explanation.surface: Describing two neighbouring parts arranged in a slow progression.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means gradually or little by little, step after step.

clue.text: Sees a new way, relaxes

indicators.note: arranging letters in a new way means rearranging them, so these words are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone finds a fresh approach and calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new way' looks like part of the phrase; 'new way' rearranges SEES A.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax tension or pressure is to lessen or loosen it, the same verb sense.
